overview: Two 1949 airgrams: one eases mail restrictions on financial instruments for commercial entrants in Japan, and one adds limited mail service to Manchuria and China via Hong Kong while curbing mail to North Korea.

people.name: Buston
people.role: Signatory of the May 1949 airgram from USPOLAD, Tokyo; otherwise unidentified

people.name: William J. Sebald
people.role: Signatory for the U.S. Political Adviser’s office in Tokyo

people.name: C. H. Boehringer
people.role: Drafter or records staff member identified by initials on both airgrams

subfiles.title: Airgram on relaxed mail restrictions for commercial entrants
subfiles.about: Reports a Far East Command announcement permitting commercial entrants to transmit financial instruments through international mail beginning June 1, 1949.
subfiles.summary: Airgram: Japan now allows mailing checks, drafts, and letters of credit, though currency stays banned; Japanese-script addresses are recommended.

subfiles.title: Airgram on mail service to North China and North Korea
subfiles.about: Reports new arrangements for surface mail from Japan to Manchuria and Chinese provinces through Hong Kong, and restrictions on mail destined for North Korea.
subfiles.summary: Airgram: Hong Kong will forward limited mail to Manchuria and China, while Japan restricts mail to North Korea.

interest: Shows 1949 occupation easing of Japan's international mail rules, amid Chinese Civil War and Korea's postal divide.
